new_candidates.body:
### Intro

Hi!

I use MuJoCo for musculoskeletal simulation, with many capsule-ellipsoid contacts, and compare MJX against MuJoCo C with a tightened `ccd_tolerance`. Doing that, I ran into the case below.

### My setup

MuJoCo 3.16.0 from PyPI, C API through the Python bindings, macOS on Apple Silicon. Also reproduced with a C build of main at c8362756.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

A capsule and an ellipsoid inside their margin get the right contact distance at `ccd_tolerance` 1e-6 and 1e-7, and a wrong one from 1e-8 down:

| ccd_tolerance | 1e-6 | 1e-7 | 1e-8 | 1e-10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.16.0 `contact.dist` | 1.98994e-5 | 1.98994e-5 | **2.31375e-5** | **2.31375e-5** |
| main `contact.dist` | 1.98994e-5 | 1.98994e-5 | **1.87524e-5** | **1.87524e-5** |

The distance of the closest points, computed independently (point-to-ellipsoid distance minimized along the capsule axis), is 1.9899368e-5 m. I expected a tighter tolerance to stay at least as close to it.

GJK runs on the capsule's axis here. On 3.16.0, by iteration 29 it has converged, but neither stop applies: `|x|` changes by 1.17e-15, just above `mjMINVAL`, and the Frank-Wolfe gap, 1.0e-16, is above `0.5 * tol^2` = 5e-17. The next step makes a nearly degenerate simplex, the distance subalgorithm moves the iterate away from the origin, `|x|` from 0.0555124272 to 0.0555156653, and that is what GJK returns. Before 7f305abd7 (3.12.0), the same kind of step dropped contacts at 1e-10 (3.3.3 to 3.11.0); its stagnation stop catches most of these, and this is one it misses. Of 600 random capsule-ellipsoid poses at known distances, 315 of them within the margin, this is the one 3.16.0 gets wrong, at every `ccd_tolerance` from 1e-8 to 1e-12.

A possible fix: the iterate cannot move away from the origin in exact arithmetic, so a step that does can be undone.

```c
// in gjk(), after x_norm = norm3(x_k); simplex, lambda, n and x_k saved before subdistance()
if (k > 0 && x_norm > x_norm_prev) {
  // restore simplex, lambda, n and x_k
  x_norm = x_norm_prev;
  break;
}
```

On 3.16.0 this fixes the distance at all 600 poses for every `ccd_tolerance` from 1e-6 to 1e-12 (largest error 4e-8 m, against 4.3e-6 m). It is not free: such steps occur at 1e-6 too, so 8 of the 600 contacts change there (the largest distance error drops from 2.5e-9 to 1.8e-10 m), and stopping early leaves 16 normals more than 1e-5 off at 1e-8 instead of 5 (the largest goes from 6e-5 to 5e-5). The distance subalgorithm may be the better place for a fix; I am happy to run these poses against one.

### Steps for reproduction

1. `pip install mujoco==3.16.0`
2. Run the script below.

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <body quat="-0.082870159271056565 -0.38233442870678819 0.82287290409712244 -0.41210812298547522">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="capsule" size="0.055992527792059175 0.036247722803144172" margin="0.0005"/>
    </body>
    <body pos="-0.035777798749378815 0.11241061696669587 -0.039297918685986907" quat="-0.0001396171787340407 -0.12623376577971315 -0.3040966018805199 0.94424058036542591">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom type="ellipsoid" size="0.078853740277202697 0.089210918938727207 0.045059853654884796" margin="0.0005"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```

</details>

### Code required for reproduction

```python
import mujoco

m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml)
d = mujoco.MjData(m)
for tol in (1e-6, 1e-7, 1e-8, 1e-10):
  m.opt.ccd_tolerance = tol
  mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
  print(f"{tol:.0e}: {d.contact[0].dist:.6e}")
```

Output on 3.16.0:

```
1e-06: 1.989937e-05
1e-07: 1.989937e-05
1e-08: 2.313753e-05
1e-10: 2.313753e-05
```

### Confirmations

- [x] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [x] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
new_candidates.title: GJK (nativeccd) returns a wrong contact distance at small ccd_tolerance, after a step onto a degenerate simplex

new_candidates.body:
### Summary

`mjc:inertia` on `MjcMeshCollisionAPI` is deprecated in favor of `newton:massModel` or `physics:approximation`, but neither can express `legacy` or `exact` mesh inertia. MuJoCo 3.16's USD decoder now warns for every authored `mjc:inertia`, and when it isn't authored, infers `convex` from the collision approximation. A USD asset therefore has to choose between a deprecation warning on every mesh and silently changed mass properties.

Checked against `mujoco` 3.16.0 source.

### Details

- The schema docs say: *"DEPRECATED: Use NewtonMassAPI's newton:massModel or UsdPhysics's physics:approximation instead."*
- `newton:massModel` only has `solid` and `shell`.
- In `ParseMjcPhysicsMeshCollisionAPI`, an authored `mjc:inertia` is honored but always triggers *"Prim '...' uses deprecated mjc:inertia. Please migrate to NewtonMassAPI's newton:massModel."*. Without it, `newton:massModel = "shell"` maps to `shell`, `physics:approximation = "convexHull"` maps to `convex`, and anything else maps to `exact`.
- As of 3.16 this runs for any mesh with `NewtonMeshCollisionAPI` or `NewtonMassAPI` (google-deepmind/mujoco#3635), not just `MjcMeshCollisionAPI`. So a mesh that previously kept the mjSpec default of `legacy` now decodes as `convex`.
- `exact` can't move to `physics:approximation = "none"` either. That tells other UsdPhysics consumers to collide with the triangle mesh, while MuJoCo always collides with the convex hull.

| MJCF `mesh/inertia` | Replacement the deprecation points to |
| --- | --- |
| `convex` | `physics:approximation = "convexHull"` |
| `shell` | `newton:massModel = "shell"` |
| `exact` | none without changing collision semantics |
| `legacy` (the MJCF default) | none |

### Why it matters

`legacy` is the default, so nearly every MJCF mesh uses it. In MuJoCo Menagerie, every mesh is `legacy` apart from 46 `shell` meshes in 3 models. Compiling each Menagerie model with its `legacy` meshes switched to `convex` changes body mass or inertia by more than 5% in 19 of the 69 model directories that have `legacy` meshes. For example, `ms_human_700` changes by up to about 320×, `flybody` by 3.3×, and `hello_robot_stretch` by 57%.

To preserve those models, newton-physics/mujoco-usd-converter#132 keeps authoring `mjc:inertia = "legacy"` (and `"exact"`). With MuJoCo 3.16's decoder, that is 889 of the 897 mesh colliders in the converted Menagerie, each emitting the deprecation warning on import.

### Request

Either of these would give converters a warning-free way to preserve `legacy` and `exact`:

1. Keep `mjc:inertia` as a supported attribute for `legacy` and `exact`, which have no replacement, and only warn for `convex` and `shell`. The deprecation note in the schema would say the same.
2. Add a non-deprecated attribute that can express `legacy` and `exact`, and point the deprecation at it.

### Reproduction

The mass difference between the default and `convex`, for a watertight non-convex mesh:

```python
import mujoco

# An L-shaped prism: non-convex and watertight, so all three volume modes apply
verts = "0 0 0  2 0 0  2 1 0  1 1 0  1 2 0  0 2 0  0 0 1  2 0 1  2 1 1  1 1 1  1 2 1  0 2 1"
faces = ("0 2 1  0 3 2  0 5 3  3 5 4  6 7 8  6 8 9  6 9 11  9 10 11  "
         "0 1 7  0 7 6  1 2 8  1 8 7  2 3 9  2 9 8  3 4 10  3 10 9  4 5 11  4 11 10  5 0 6  5 6 11")
for inertia in ("legacy", "convex", "exact"):
    xml = f"""<mujoco><asset><mesh name="l" inertia="{inertia}" vertex="{verts}" face="{faces}"/></asset>
    <worldbody><body><freejoint/><geom type="mesh" mesh="l"/></body></worldbody></mujoco>"""
    m = mujoco.MjSpec.from_string(xml).compile()
    print(f"{inertia:>6}: mass {m.body_mass[1]:.1f} kg, inertia {m.body_inertia[1].round(1)}")
```

```
legacy: mass 3000.0 kg, inertia [1833.3 1500.   833.3]
convex: mass 3500.0 kg, inertia [2103.2 1583.3 1103.2]
 exact: mass 3000.0 kg, inertia [1833.3 1500.   833.3]
```

The decoder behavior above comes from reading `plugin/usd_decoder/usd_decoder.cc` at 3.16.0, not from a native USD round trip.
new_candidates.title: USD: mjc:inertia is deprecated, but legacy and exact mesh inertia have no replacement
